name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '_51' is dispatch idx 0x51 (xref site 0x51CD5), a genuine domain dispatch-slot ID, not address residue. Descriptor corrected from '__unref_dyn_turn_event' to '__ch30_boss_defeat_pump': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch30 kill-drop path -- ch30 char_spawn_records[1..4] = the endgame bosses (enemy_data 54..57, char_id 0x7A..0x7D, lv30..40) each carry pickup_kind=2 param=0x51, so each boss's death dispatches consequence[0x51], a self-looping pump that advances the stage counter and re-schedules the turn-event to drive the endgame sequence. The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path.
purpose: Chapter 30 endgame boss-defeat pump (dispatch idx 0x51, reached via the ch30 kill-drop path when an endgame boss records[1..4] enemy_data 54..57, pickup_kind=2 param=0x51, falls): a self-looping pump that advances the tile-event stage counter and queues another turn-event fire one player turn ahead, driving the ch30 endgame sequence forward.
logic_summary: Two stores after the Watcom __CHK stack-probe prologue: (1) INC the 8-bit stage counter at tile_event_consumed_flags[0x10] (INC byte ptr [EAX+0x10]); (2) read battle_turn_counter as a single byte, INC it in 8-bit (MOV DL,[turn_counter] / INC DL), and store the truncated result into tile_event_data_table[+3] (hook entry 0's turn byte), arming the next fire one player turn ahead. No consume-flag gate (unlike gated schedulers handler_3e/41), so each call advances the stage and re-arms the same hook slot. event_arg is unread.

params.reason: Matches the shared 1-arg cdecl dispatch signature used by all sibling chapter_event_handler functions; descriptive, no address residue. Arg is unused but the name correctly reflects the dispatch-table contract.

returns.semantics: No return value; pure state-machine mutator.

data_fd2_tile_event_data_table_ptr (0x53A55; base of turn-event hook table, written at +3)
